response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_reb, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net FROM fees GROUP BY orderslink), bench AS (SELECT AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS b FROM fees) SELECT AVG(p.avg_reb) AS avg_of_avg_rebtotal, AVG(p.avg_net) AS avg_of_avg_net_fee_rate, AVG(p.avg_net - bench.b) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN bench WHERE p.avg_net > bench.b

assumptions.assumption: Fee records with NULL orderslink are grouped together as one group (GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group), and that group is treated like any other order.
A fee record's net rate is NULL if either feerate or rebrate is NULL, so it is skipped in the net-rate averages. Rebate averages skip NULL rebtotal separately.
If no group exceeds the benchmark, the query returns one row of NULLs.
